slots.brief: Zener diode in series with a resistor across a DC supply; circuit diagram given; find current through/load voltage or power dissipated in the Zener
Rigid rod or ladder in equilibrium; find torque about a chosen point to get an unknown force
Two point charges fixed, find null point position where field is zero
Given wave equation y = A sin(kx − ωt), read amplitude, frequency, wavelength, and wave speed
Find point on screen where path difference is λ/4; compute resulting intensity relative to Imax
rms speed scaling with molar mass at same temperature; compare two gases
Monatomic gas heat added at constant volume; find temperature rise using first law
Position vector given as function of time; differentiate to get velocity/acceleration at an instant
Magnetization vs field diagram for dia/para/ferromagnetic material; identify type from curve or susceptibility sign
Photon emitted in transition between two levels of hydrogen-like ion (Z given); compute its energy
Particle moving in a straight line; find angular momentum about a fixed off-line point using r × p magnitude
Given B amplitude of EM wave, find E amplitude using E = cB
Solid floats at interface between two liquids with given fraction immersed; compare densities or find density of body
Wheatstone bridge with one unknown resistance; use balance condition to find it, or find equivalent resistance of unbalanced bridge
Fraction/mass remaining after n half-lives; count half-lives from given total time
Two parallel wires with given currents; find net field at a point midway or at a specified location
Blocks in contact or connected by string on frictionless surface; find acceleration then contact/tension force
Block on incline with applied force shown in diagram; find range of force for equilibrium given friction coefficient
Series capacitor combination with dielectric slab inserted; from circuit diagram find new charge, voltage division, or energy
Simple pendulum moved to a place where g changes; find % change in period or new frequency
Two-stage motion or average speed with equal distances at two speeds; set up simultaneous equations
Wire stretched by two loads; find new length/elongation using Y = stress/strain, watch area change
Loop with changing area or entering/leaving a field region as per diagram; compute induced emf via dΦ/dt

slots.chapter: Dual Nature of Radiation and Matter
slots.brief: de Broglie wavelength comparison of electron and proton at same KE, or accelerated through same potential
Express a physical quantity (e.g., from an unfamiliar named formula) in base units and identify its dimensional formula
Perfectly inelastic collision of two bodies; find common velocity and KE loss
Variation of g with height/depth; compare g at altitude vs surface, or find height where g drops by given fraction
Ice/water mixture with heat loss/gain plus phase change; find final temperature or fraction melted
Lens immersed in a medium of given refractive index; use lens-maker relation to find new focal length and nature of lens
Give four small molecules/ions with their shapes and ask which one has a shape different from the rest (e.g. three bent, one linear or vice versa); pure VSEPR recall, no numbers.
List four ordering statements about first ionisation enthalpies across a period or down a group (including a Be/B or N/O type anomaly) and ask which statement is wrong.
Ask which of the given aqueous ions (e.g. Sc3+, Ti3+, Cu+, Zn2+, V3+) is colourless and why, or which listed ion shows a stated colour.
Show a two-step sequence from phenol or anisole (structures drawn in the figure) through a named intermediate and ask for the final product structure; keep steps to standard textbook reagents.
Present 3–4 statements on structures/hybridisation/hydrolysis of XeF2, XeF4, XeF6 (and their hydrolysis products) and ask how many are correct; make one statement subtly wrong on hydrolysis.
Give stopping potential vs frequency graphs for two metals (figure) and ask for the comparison of work functions or the value of h from the slope; simple plug-in after reading the graph.
Ask for the number and location of tetrahedral and octahedral voids in an fcc unit cell, possibly counting how many lattice atoms enclose a given void type.
Ask which radical species initiates ozone decomposition in the stratosphere and identify the catalytic chain steps; include one statement about CFCs vs NOx.
Draw the structure of a substituted cycloalkene or alkene (figure) and ask for the carbonyl fragment(s) obtained after ozonolysis with reductive workup.
Give a transition metal ion (e.g. Mn2+ or Cr3+ or Fe3+), ask for its d-electron configuration, count of unpaired electrons, and the spin-only moment in BM using √(n(n+2)).
Numerical where a fixed half-life must be used to find the time for a sample to fall from an initial to a final mass/activity — count the number of half-lives and multiply.
Give ΔH (or ΔU) for a reaction involving gaseous species and ask for ΔU (or ΔH) using ΔH = ΔU + Δng RT; one-step computation with R = 8.314.

For a sparingly soluble salt of a given dissolution equation (e.g. with 2:1 stoichiometry), relate solubility s to Ksp, then compute either s from Ksp or Ksp from s; also compare solubilities of two salts with same/different stoichiometry.

Give the observed molar mass of a complex salt in solution (or its measured boiling point elevation) and ask to deduce the dissociation/association and hence the number of ions or the formula of the complex.
Ask why aryl/vinyl halides fail in Williamson synthesis, or which of the given haloalkane + alkoxide pairs gives ether cleanly vs elimination; test the conceptual condition.
Give four carbanions (methyl vs substituted/hybridised variations, e.g. sp3 vs sp2 vs sp C−) and ask to rank their stability.
Show a Fischer projection of a molecule with four different groups (figure) and ask for the R/S configuration at the stereocentre, with one distractor being a 180° rotation of the projection.
Ask for the therapeutic class or target use of a well-known NCERT-listed drug (e.g. equanil, terfenadine, cimetidine); one correct classification among four options.
Give a described observation (e.g. violet colour with iodine, red Cu2O with Tollens'/Fehling's, or osazone formation) and ask which sugar/disaccharide test it corresponds to.
Rank or pick the odd one out among given amines in aqueous basicity (aliphatic vs aniline vs ammonia type comparison); purely conceptual, no pKa values.
Given a change in T and P for the same gas (or a comparison of two gases), find the new density or the ratio of densities using ρ = PM/RT; medium algebra but no unit traps.
For a simple one-electron or two-electron half-cell (e.g. metal ion concentration given at 298 K), compute the electrode potential using the Nernst equation; straightforward plug-in.
Draw an ester structure (figure), treat with two equivalents of a Grignard reagent followed by acid workup, and ask which tertiary alcohol forms (distractors from single-addition products).
Give a formula of a simple coordination compound (e.g. ammine/aqua/chloro complex with a cation or anionic complex) and ask for its correct IUPAC name among four close options.
Give a complex with a specified ligand set (strong-field vs weak-field) and ask for the number of unpaired electrons (optionally the spin-only moment) in its high-spin/low-spin form.
Give E°cell (and n) for a reaction and compute ΔG°; alternatively use ΔG° = −nFE° = −RT ln K to find the equilibrium constant sign or magnitude for the given cell.
Ask about inversion/retention and racemisation for a chiral substrate under SN1 vs SN2 conditions, or which substrate/conditions lead to racemisation.
Give volumes and molarities of an acid and a base (with clear stoichiometry like HCl vs NaOH) and ask for the volume of one needed for complete neutralisation of the other.

Using the Rydberg relation, ask for the ratio or value of wavelength/energy for a transition in Lyman or Balmer, e.g. compare the n=2→1 and n=3→2 lines via 1/λ scaling; harder reasoning, so make the algebra slightly involved.
Draw four cyclic species in the figure (e.g. cyclopentadienyl anion, tropylium cation, cyclooctatetraene) and ask which are aromatic, with answer as a code of correct options.
Two-blank sentence with a contrasting conjunction (e.g., 'although'); student must pick the pair where both words fit the logical direction of the clause.
Sentence where the subject is separated from its verb by an intervening phrase; error is the verb's number agreement.
Ask for the meaning of a common figurative idiom (e.g., 'to let the cat out of the bag') in a short context sentence.
Single-blank simple sentence; choose the one clearly fitting word from four straightforward options.
Ask the nearest meaning of a low-frequency/literary word; distractors are near-synonyms that differ in register or shade of meaning.
Four-sentence jumble about a general topic; pick the correct opening sentence that introduces the subject without pronoun/connector dependencies.
Short sentence with a wrong verb-preposition collocation; student identifies the preposition as the error. Keep all other parts grammatical.
Ask the opposite of a simple, high-frequency adjective; options are all plausible antonym-style words but only one is correct.
Mixed letter-number series where letters shift by a fixed step and numbers follow their own rule; ask for the next term.
Arrange four simple words in dictionary order; words chosen so only the 2nd or 3rd letter breaks ties.
Two straightforward universal statements and four conclusions; test basic All/Some deduction with Venn logic.
Three words coded in different code strings; identify codes of common words by comparing letters across messages.
A points to B saying 'he is the son of my grandfather's only son'; decode a short two-step chain to find the relation.
Ask which given word cannot be formed using the letters of a supplied longer word, with one distractor requiring a repeated letter.
A word is coded by shifting each letter by a position-based pattern (e.g., +1, +2, +3...); apply the same rule to a new word.
Describe a small family with siblings and cousins; ask how many males/females or how many members of a particular relation exist.
Repeating block of letters (e.g., a cycle of 4-5 letters with gaps); fill the blank positions in the sequence.
Pair like 'ACE : 135 :: BD? : ?' style — map letters to positional values and find the matching number group; include a twist in the second mapping rule.
Statements mixing All and Some with negatives; conclusions include possibility cases ('...being a possibility is true'), two of which look close.
Four letter/number pairs where three share a hidden rule (e.g., same positional difference or reversal); pick the pair that breaks it.
Direct (1 − cos x)/x²-type standard trig limit at 0 using known standard limits; ask the value.
Count the number of possible skew-symmetric 3×3 matrices with entries from a small given set; use the zero diagonal constraint.
Given an infinite GP sum relation like a + ar + … = expression in a, take logs to find the common ratio r.
Find the locus of z satisfying arg((z − α)/(z − β)) = π/2; derive the circle with α, β as endpoints of a diameter.
Given a function built with the greatest integer function, invert (or restrict) to determine which values are excluded from its range.
Select a committee of a given size from men and women with a minimum/maximum gender constraint; count cases by composition.
For a quadratic or cubic restricted to an interval, decide the largest interval on which it is bijective/invertible using monotonicity.
Given the mean of n observations, find the new mean after each observation is scaled and shifted (axᵢ + b).
Find the sum of coefficients of odd/even-power terms in a product of two binomial expansions using x = 1 and x = −1 subtraction.

slots.subtopic: Image of a point in a line
slots.brief: Reflect a given point in a given line using the foot-of-perpendicular midpoint idea; ask for the image coordinates.
Definite integral of f(x)/(f(x)+f(a−x)) type; apply King's property to halve the integral and evaluate at level 4 difficulty.
Piecewise function with a parameter k at the joining point; set one-sided limits equal to find k for continuity.
Find intervals where a simple polynomial or x³ − 3x-type function is increasing/decreasing using the sign of f′(x).
Given a homogeneous second-degree equation representing two lines, find the angle between them using the tan θ formula with a, b, h.
Circle of fixed radius whose centre moves while remaining tangent to both a line and a circle (or two fixed lines); find the locus of the centre.
Compute an expression of the form (z + z̄)/|z|² or similar, then raise to a power using De Moivre; ask for the real part or modulus.
Find the domain of a function combining a square root with a rational expression; use a sign chart and interval union.
System of three equations with a parameter; find the value for which it has infinitely many solutions by checking Δ = 0 and consistency.
Solve a homogeneous dy/dx = f(y/x) by substituting y = vx; separate variables and integrate to get the general solution.
Semi-latus rectum / focal chord length of a standard parabola; recall latus rectum length = 2·(distance focus–directrix) and apply directly.
Find the foot of the perpendicular from a point to a plane (or from a point to a line in 3D); then compute the required distance.
Evaluate ∫eˣ(f(x) + f′(x)) dx over a definite interval by recognising it equals eˣf(x).
Find the chord of contact of tangents drawn from an external point to a circle, then use it to compute a length or prove a pole-polar property at level 4 difficulty.
Decompose a proper rational function (distinct linear factors) into partial fractions and integrate each term.
Given a family of curves y = ax² + bx (two arbitrary constants), differentiate twice and eliminate a, b to form the differential equation.
Given the variance of a data set, find the variance after each observation is multiplied by a constant and shifted; test the invariance under shifting.

slots.subtopic: Range of a sin + b cos
slots.brief: Find the range of a sin θ + b cos θ + c and decide which value in the options lies outside it.
Given compound statements built with ∧, ∨, negations, identify which option is logically equivalent to the given statement; simplify with De Morgan's laws.
For a quadratic with given roots, evaluate a symmetric expression like 1/α + 1/β or α²β + αβ² using Vieta's relations.
For a cubic, find the point of inflexion by setting f″(x) = 0 and verifying the sign change of f″.
Evaluate tan⁻¹(something like 1/2) + tan⁻¹(1/3)-style compositions or sin(tan⁻¹ x) using the right-triangle method.
Find the area enclosed between two parabolas by locating intersection points and integrating the difference.
Draw one card/ball from a well-defined set; compute P(A ∪ B) from given individual and joint probabilities using the addition rule.

Two-factory / urn partition problem: given total probabilities of a defect, use Bayes' theorem to find the posterior probability of the source; ask for the exact posterior value at level 4 difficulty.
Evaluate cos α + cos(α+d) + … + cos(α + (n−1)d) using the telescoping sine-difference formula; ask for the closed form.
Express one vector as a linear combination of the other two by equating components; solve the resulting simultaneous equations for the scalars.
Two lines through the origin with given direction vectors; find the direction cosines of the (acute) angle bisector using the sum of unit vectors.
Given position vectors of triangle vertices, compute side lengths via dot/magnitude and classify the triangle (right/isoceles).
Simple related-rates problem, e.g. rate of increase of a circle's area given the rate of radius increase; differentiate A = πr².
For a matrix of the form I + A with A² = A (or nilpotent A), derive a closed form for (I + A)^n and evaluate a specific power using the pattern.
